name: Pale blush
lede: Pale blush is a muted, warm beige-pink, built by putting the modifier pale in front of the base color [[blush]].

sections.title: A modifier on blush
sections.body:
Pale blush puts the modifier word pale in front of the base color [[blush]], in the compound-modifier grammar our library uses for names like this one [1]. Both the Inter-Society Color Council's 1955 ISCC-NBS system and Robert Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* carry this swatch, though our data does not give the exact plate for this entry [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[sweet-pea]], only 3.3 units off, close enough on screen to read as the same warm pink-beige [2]; [[light-brownish-vinaceous]] and [[rose-dawn]] sit within 4.5 units [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive finds a color within range of this swatch in 381 of 23,781 paintings, 1.6 percent, as photographed; looking for real coverage inside each painting narrows that to 255 [3]. That makes it more common than 74 percent of the named colors in our library [3]. It most often plays a hidden color, in 47 percent of its 255 appearances by lightness rank, meaning it tends to sit in a shadow or a mixed tone rather than a bold patch [3].

The earliest match dates to the year 900, over a thousand years before Ridgway's 1912 plate, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin; it marks a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not a surviving pigment or dye [3]. In printed English the word blush rose fastest around 1800, well before this specific compound name was standardized [3].
